This gel has a funny smell and I needed to apply it way more often than I did the Aquaphor. In the end, its convenient that the tube is small and can pretty much fit in your back pocket, but I don't think I will buy it again.

Feels expensive and gimmicky, but I honestly can't complain all that much given the awesome results - the colors on my tattoo settled vibrantly and I still get compliments on them months later.  Great relief, but something tells me another product would have done just fine - I just didn't fell like shopping for a lotion that would be safe on tattoos when this was readily available.

reviews.t: It's okay, but I'll stick with the cream next time
reviews.x: I've use other H2Ocean products for my tatts, and decided to give this one a go. It definitely "seals" the new tatt, but it leaves my skin a bit greasy. I ended up applying H2Ocean's regular cream (or Lubriderm when that ran out) on top of it to keep the greasy stuff from getting on my clothes.

Thinner consistency than aquaphor which makes it gone in nicer.  Not sticky or greasy and Very hydrating and my tattoo looks amazing after healing.  I keep it in my purse and just use it it to hydrate my tattoos when necessary

This is by far the best tattoo stuff I've ever used. I have over 20 tats and this stuff is amazing. Helps heal quickly, didn't irritate my sensitive skin, and a little bit goes a long way! So glad I found this product.
It keep my tattoo hydrated, kept  it from itching and pealing.

Both samples worked pretty well, so when I went to re order some after care cream, the H2Ocean was a little less expensive than the After Inked. For the first week, this is an essential!  I use this moisturizer after  washing with only the gentle foamy soap by Aquatat.  Without these two products, my tattoos are impossibly itchy and took twice as long to heal.  I have found nothing that works as well.  These are must haves.  Have them on hand, before you get your next tattoo so you will be ready.

My tattoo artist used this during the tattoo process and I used it as aftercare afterwards. It went on easy, spread easy, and kept the tattoo protected well in harsh winter conditions. Colors stayed in with no problems and for the first time ever I had no cracking during the late stages of the healing process.

OMG I used this for a few days on my new tat, and I have had a terrible reaction! My leg is broken out, I'm now having to take antihistamines, Steriods, and use hydrocortisone cream! I've paid more to the Dr. and for meds than my tat! BEWARE! Look at the ingredients!

claims.text: Many reviewers say it helps tattoos heal quickly and effectively.
Reviewers frequently report that it soothes itching and keeps tattoos hydrated.
Several reviewers prefer its thinner, less greasy consistency over Aquaphor and find it easy to apply.
A few reviewers find it greasy, oddly scented, or no better than alternatives, and some question whether it's necessary.
Some reviewers note it leaves skin greasy and requires more frequent reapplication.
